children: Shares of quantum computing company IonQ

fell 8.8% in the afternoon session after the company announced an agreement to acquire cybersecurity company Elisity in an all-stock deal valued at up to $1.3 billion. According to the company press release, the price includes up to $150 million that depends on Elisity’s results. The share count will be set off IonQ’s 20-day average price before closing, inside a collar of $33.07 to $49.61 a share. The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter, subject to regulatory approval.

Elisity has more than 100 customer deployments, and IonQ said the business has doubled revenue and its customer base year over year with no churn among deployed customers. The combination pairs IonQ’s post-quantum cryptography and quantum key distribution with Elisity’s Zero Trust software, aimed at a microsegmentation market IonQ put at more than $10 billion. According to TipRanks, the all-stock structure raised dilution concerns, and the selling spread to D-Wave, Rigetti, and Quantum Computing Inc. TipRanks also tied the pressure to a 10-year Treasury yield that recently moved above 5.3%.
What Is The Market Telling Us

IonQ’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 79 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 19 days ago when the stock gained 4.8% on the news that the company announced an end-to-end real-time quantum error correction decoder that runs on a single standard central processing unit. The technology eliminates classical decoding delays that previously caused quantum hardware to pause during operations. IonQ verified the decoder across circuits simulating up to 408 logical qubits and more than 31.5 million quantum operations. In addition, IonQ announced that its Superion 256 quantum computer will serve as the first on-premise quantum deployment at NVIDIA's Accelerated Quantum Research Center, linking directly to an NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 system via NVIDIA NVQLink.

IonQ is down 22.9% since the beginning of the year, and at $36.06 per share, it is trading 56.1% below its 52-week high of $82.09 from October 2025. Despite the year-to-date decline, investors who bought $1,000 worth of IonQ’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $4,227.

Nvidia’s chips cost a hundred grand. The connectors that make them work cost even more. One company makes them all.

Every AI server needs specialized infrastructure the chip companies don’t make. High-speed cables. Power connectors. Thermal sensors. This 90-year-old company built a monopoly on it. The AI boom just started. This stock is still flying under the radar.
